cliModal.extraNotesPinning: This command is only for local pinning/unpinning. If you want to use a remote pinning service, consult that service's documentation to learn how to pin/unpin from the command line.

shareModal.title: Share files
shareModal.description: Copy the link below and share it with your friends.
shareModal.descriptionLocal: Use this link to open in apps running on this machine.
shareModal.descriptionNative: This native IPFS address opens in apps and browsers that support IPFS, like the <1>IPFS Companion</1> extension.
shareModal.useLocalLink: Local HTTP link for other apps on this machine
shareModal.useSubdomains: Use localhost subdomains for web apps
shareModal.linkError: Could not generate the link. Check that your IPFS node is running.
shareModal.contentIdentity: An IPFS CID identifies content-addressed bytes. An IPNS name can point to changing content. A display name or filename in the link does not change the content address.
shareModal.availability: A link does not guarantee availability or keep content online. Retrieval needs a node or service that still provides the requested bytes. A local link is usable only where that local gateway is reachable.
shareModal.accessControl: A CID is not a password or access-control rule. Someone who obtains it may request available bytes through a permitted node or gateway. Choose confidentiality protections separately.
shareModal.encryption: Sharing a CID does not encrypt or decrypt anything. If the content was encrypted before it was added, the CID addresses encrypted bytes; reading the plaintext requires the right decryption key and software. The CID itself does not provide that key.

removeModal.checkboxUnpinFromServicesScope: Also request unpinning from configured remote services
removeModal.mfsRetention: This removes the selected MFS path names. It does not immediately delete all underlying blocks. Content referenced by another MFS path or protected by a pin can remain; unreferenced, unpinned blocks may later be reclaimed by local garbage collection. Other nodes or services may retain copies.
removeModal.localPinHelp: If MFS removal succeeds, this also requests removal of the corresponding local pin. Unpinning changes retention protection; it is not immediate block deletion.
removeModal.remotePinHelp: If MFS removal succeeds, this also requests unpinning from the named services listed below. It does not delete copies throughout IPFS or change a service’s own retention policy.
removeModal.localPinRequested: Local scope: remove the selected MFS paths and request removal of their local pins where reported pinned.
removeModal.localPinUnchanged: Local scope: remove the selected MFS paths; no local pin removal is requested.
removeModal.remoteServicesRequested: Remote scope: also request unpinning from these configured services:
removeModal.noRemoteTargets: No configured remote service targets are listed for this request.
removeModal.remotePinsUnchanged: Remote scope: no remote pin removal is requested.

pinningModal.title: Select where you would like to pin these items.
pinningModal.footer: Need to add or configure a pinning service? Go to <1>Settings</1>.
pinningModal.retentionHelp: Each selection controls pin retention at the named location. Unpinning is not block deletion or removal of copies from the IPFS network. Pin selection does not remove MFS paths.
pinningModal.localRemoval: Local change: request removal of this node’s pin. Data may remain protected by MFS or other pins; unprotected blocks may later be reclaimed by local garbage collection.
pinningModal.remoteOnlyRemoval: The listed removals affect remote services; this node’s local pin selection and MFS paths are unchanged.
pinningModal.remoteRemoval: Request pin removal from these named remote services. Remote requests affect only those services; any selected local change is listed separately. Deletion or retention at a service is not guaranteed:
pinningModal.localAddition: Local change: request adding a pin on this node. Any remote pin removals listed below are separate requests.
pinningModal.localUnknown: Local pin state is not reported. Review the Local node selection separately from the remote service choices.

step1.title: Files page
step1.paragraph1: <0>This is where the files on your <1>Mutable File System (MFS)</1> live. You can add files or folders and manage them from this page.</0>

step2.title: Breadcrumbs
step2.paragraph1: These breadcrumbs display the path to your current directory. You can…
step2.bullet1: Click an individual breadcrumb to go to that directory
step2.bullet2: Right-click a breadcrumb to get the actions menu for that directory
step2.bullet3: Drag files onto a breadcrumb to move or import them

step3.title: Add files
step3.paragraph1: Here you can see how many blocks and files you have pinned.
step3.paragraph2: You can add files or folders to your repo through the dropdown on the right.
step3.paragraph3: <0>If you want to add something that is already on IPFS, you can import it to your MFS by passing its <1>Content Identifier (CID)</1>.</0>

step5.title: Files list
step5.paragraph1: Finally, the listing where you can find your files and folders. Drag and drop files or folders to add them.
step5.paragraph2: You can share or download files, inspect them in the IPLD Explorer, rename or remove them.
step5.paragraph3: Pro tip: drag and drop a file from any other page of the Web UI to add them to the root of your MFS.

step6.title: Files grid
step6.paragraph1: The grid view displays your files and folders as thumbnails, making it easy to visually browse your content.
step6.paragraph2: You can share or download files, inspect them in the IPLD Explorer, rename or remove them.

previewLimitReached: This preview is limited to 10 KiB. Click the download button to access the full file.
localDatastoreDescription: Total size of all blocks currently stored in the Datastore of your IPFS node (“RepoSize” from “ipfs repo stat”). This includes everything in the Files view (MFS), low-level pins, and any recently removed or temporary cached blocks that were not garbage-collected yet.
currentLocationDescription: Total size of the DAG behind the current directory (“CumulativeSize” from “ipfs files stat”). This value includes both local and remote blocks, and could be bigger than the size of your local datastore.
cidNotFileNorDir: The current link isn't a file, nor a directory. Try to <1>inspect</1> it instead.
